questions.question: What are simple phenolics and polyphenolics? / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• What are simple phenolics and polyphenolics?
  • Simple phenolics – containing single phenol group. They include simple phenols, phenolic acids and
  • coumarins. Polyphenolics – containing more than one phenolic groups. They include flavonoids
  • tannins and lignans.

questions.question: Explain the extraction chamber of a Soxhlet apparatus / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the extraction chamber of a Soxhlet apparatus
  • a wide tube with same width at the top while the bottom is closed. In this chamber the plant material
  • is placed. The extraction chamber has 2 siphons attached. The Vapour distillation path arise from the
  • base stem and connects to the top region of the extraction chamber. The small siphon tube is a U
  • shaped tube that arise from the base of the extraction tube, runs up half of the extraction tube and then
  • runs down as a U and then opens in to round bottom.
  • [U] / [CO2]

questions.question: What is partition coefficient? How K value of a phytochemical determine solubility / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• What is partition coefficient? How K value of a phytochemical determine solubility
  • It equals the concentration of solute in the organic phase divided by its concentration in the aqueous
  • phase. K > 1: The phytochemical is lipophilic; K < 1: The phytochemical is hydrophilic

questions.question: Explain the biosynthesis of carbohydrate / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain the biosynthesis of carbohydrate
  • Photosynthesis- capture sunlight through chlorophyll. The light-dependent reactions generate ATP and
  • NADPH, which are then used in the Calvin cycle to fix atmo spheric CO₂ into simple sugars.
  • Gluconeogenesis: The process of synthesizing glucose fro m non -carbohydrate sources like lactate,
  • pyruvate, glycerol, and certain amino acids. Glycogenesis - Once glucose is synthesized, animals store
  • excess glucose as glyco gen, plants convert these sugars into sucrose for transport, starch for stora ge
  • and cellulose for structural support in cell walls.

questions.question: Explain manual grinding and knife-blade-hammer grinding / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain manual grinding and knife-blade-hammer grinding
  • Manual- sample is manually crushed and ground using Mortar and Pestle. Often inert abrasives, such
  • as washed sand glass beads are added. Knife-blade-hammer- bulk processing of dried plant biomass
  • (barks, roots, stems, dried leaves). a) Blade/Cutting Mills: Use sharp rotating blades to chop fiber-rich
  • materials (like stems and leaves) into uniform, coarse fragments. b) Blender – Blender can be used to
  • grind both fresh and dried plant samples. c) Hammer Mills: Use heavy mechanical "hammers" hitting
  • at high speeds to crush brittle, dense elements like dry roots and wood into fine powders.
  • [U] / [CO2]

questions.question: Explain the principle and procedure of Bradford's method of protein determination / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• .
  • Explain the principle and procedure of Bradford's method of protein determination
  • The assay relies on the binding of a dye called Coomassie Brilliant Blue G -250 to proteins. Under
  • highly acidic condit ions, the dye is naturally in a doubly protonated red/brown state. When the dye
  • binds to proteins, it converts into a stable blue, unprotonated form. This blue protein -dye complex
  • shows maximum absorbance at 595 nm. The increase in absorbance at 595 nm is directly proportional
  • to the amount of protein present. Add 1 mL of the sample to a test tube. To control tube add 1 ml
  • distilled water. To both tubes, add 1 ml of Bradford reagent. Mix the contents and keep it aside for 10
  • minutes. Observe the colour chan ge and take the reading using a spectrophotometer at 595 nm with
  • control tube as blank
  • [U] / [CO3]

questions.question: Explain Hager's test and Mayer's test for the detection of alkaloids / [CO3]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain Hager's test and Mayer's test for the detection of alkaloids
  • Mayers Test- Nitrogen atoms in basic alkaloids form coordinate bonds or insoluble complexes with
  • potassium-mercuric ions. This results in the formation of a cream -colored or pale yellow precipitate.
  • Take 2 ml of a given sample in a clean, dry test tube. Add 2 ml of concentrated HCl to both the tubes
  • and mix them. Add 5 drops of Mayer’s Reagent. The emergence of a white precipitate or a distinct
  • green coloration serves as a positive confirmation for the presence of alkaloid compounds.
  • Hager’s Test- Picric acid acts as an organic acid that forms crystalline picrate salts with basic alkaloid
  • molecules. Take 2 ml of a given sample in a clean, dry test tube. Add 6 drops of Hagers's Reagent. Mix
  • well. The formation of an yellow precipitate indicate the presence of alkaloids
  • [U] / [CO3]

questions.question: What is solvent-solvent extraction? Explain co-current method. / [CO4]
questions.solution_html:
• What is solvent-solvent extraction? Explain co-current method.
  • the crude plant extract dissolved in a solvent is treated with another pure immiscible solvent. This helps
  • to transfer the compound on interest or the impurities into the fresh immiscible solvent. In a co-current
  • (or forward -flow) solvent -solvent extraction mechanism, the feed solution (containing the target
  • metabolite) and the immiscible extracting solvent travel through the extraction system in the same
  • direction. It is useful for fast, equilibrium-limited, or reactive extractions where pr olonged contact is
  • undesirable. The mechanism relies on a repeating cycle of stages. Each stage consists of two distinct
  • physical phases: Mixing (Mass Transfer) and Settling (Phase Separation).
  • [U] / [CO4]

questions.question: Write an essay on Ultrasound assisted extraction and Super Critical Fluid extraction / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Write an essay on Ultrasound assisted extraction and Super Critical Fluid extraction
  • Ultrasound assisted extraction- Ultrasound-assisted extraction (UAE) is a green, non-thermal technique
  • that uses high-frequency, high-intensity sound waves to recover valuable secondary plant metabolites
  • (such as phenolics, flavo noids, alkaloids, and esse ntial oils) from plant matrices. Principle - Acoustic
  • Cavitation. Bubble Formation: Low -frequency ultrasound waves (typically 20 kHz to several MHz)
  • pass through a liquid solvent containing immersed plant material. Cavitation: The pressure cycles create
  • microscopic vacuum bubbles that grow and violently collapse. Cell Disruption: The collapse generates
  • localized high temperatures, high pressures, and intense shear forces. These forces break plant cell
  • walls and membranes, accelerating the release of intracellular metabolites into the solvent
  • Super Critical Fluid extraction- separation technique that uses a fluid in a supercritical state (meaning
  • it is kept at a temperature and pressure above its critical point where liquid and gas phases merge) —to
  • dissolve and isolate specific target compounds from a solid or liquid matrix. A gas like carbon dioxide
  • (CO₂) is pressurized and heated past its critical point, giving it gas-like diffusion properties and liquid-
  • like dissolving power (Supercritical fluid). The supercritical fluid flows through a high-pressure vessel
  • holding the raw material to dissolve the desired components. The system reduces pressure in a separator
  • vessel, turning the CO₂ back into a gas so it releases the extracted product for collection.
  • [K] / [CO2]

questions.question: Explain vertical gel electrophoresis / [CO4] [10x1 = 10]
questions.solution_html:
• Explain vertical gel electrophoresis
  • Separation of charged molecules like proteins and short nucleic acid through a vertically placed gel.
  • Gel made of Poly acrylamide (Acrylamide, bis acrylamides, APS and TEMED). Two gels- Resolving
  • gel and stacking gel. Stacking gel (highly porous layer with a pH of 6.8) stack the proteins and resolving
  • gel (dense layer with a higher pH of 8.8) separates protein based on charge and mass. Native PAGE -
  • separation based on charge and mass, SDS - separation based on mass only - SDS non-reductive and
  • SDS reductive PAGE. Stacking gel low voltage, for resolving gel, enhance the voltage. Buffer system
  • TAE or TBE buffer. Once tracking dye reaches the end, electrophoresis is stopped and the gel is stained
  • and viewed.
  • [U] / [CO4]
  • [10x1 = 10]
